description: One row per trajectory timestep. Encodes motion state + directional spatial affordance. Targets are next-step displacements (no leakage). Last timestep of each trajectory is excluded.

normalization.u_v: global MinMax over dataset world_x / world_y extents
normalization.dist_features: divided by map-wide max: obs=26.1840 m, bnd=24.1688 m
normalization.du_dv_speed: raw metres/step — scale at training time with a split-fitted scaler to avoid leakage

trajectory_id.reason: Groups timesteps belonging to the same person; required for sequential modelling and evaluation split

timestep.interpretation: Position within the trajectory; 0 = first step
timestep.reason: Allows absolute positioning within a sequence without encoding recording artifacts of raw frame numbers

u.interpretation: World x position normalised by dataset-wide extents
u.reason: Gives the model a stable positional reference; global normalisation keeps positions comparable across trajectories

v.interpretation: World y position normalised by dataset-wide extents
v.reason: Same as u for the vertical axis

du.interpretation: World x displacement from the previous timestep; 0 at first step
du.reason: Encodes instantaneous horizontal velocity without positional bias; primary motion signal for the model

dv.interpretation: World y displacement from the previous timestep; 0 at first step
dv.reason: Same as du for the vertical axis

speed.interpretation: Euclidean magnitude of (du, dv); redundant with du+dv but explicit
speed.reason: Explicit speed lets the model attend to magnitude separately from direction. Kept despite derivability because LSTMs benefit from pre-computed magnitude to avoid learning sqrt implicitly.

heading_sin.interpretation: sin(atan2(dv, du)); part of unit-vector heading encoding
heading_sin.reason: Sine+cosine encoding avoids the discontinuity at ±π that a raw angle would create, giving the model a smooth heading representation

turn_rate.interpretation: Signed change in heading from previous timestep; 0 at first step
turn_rate.reason: Captures angular dynamics (curved vs straight paths). Important for distinguishing intentional turns from noise.

dist_to_obstacle_norm.interpretation: Distance from the agent's plan-pixel position to the nearest obstacle, divided by map maximum (26.184 m)
dist_to_obstacle_norm.reason: Spatial affordance signal; low values indicate the agent is near an obstacle

dist_to_boundary_norm.interpretation: Distance to the walkable-area boundary, divided by map maximum (24.169 m)
dist_to_boundary_norm.reason: Complements dist_to_obstacle: captures proximity to the edge of the navigable region

delta_dist_to_obstacle.interpretation: Change in dist_to_obstacle_norm from previous step; 0 at first step
delta_dist_to_obstacle.reason: Encodes approach/retreat dynamics relative to obstacles. Helps the model anticipate avoidance manoeuvres before the agent is already close.

delta_dist_to_boundary.interpretation: Change in dist_to_boundary_norm from previous step; 0 at first step
delta_dist_to_boundary.reason: Same as delta_dist_to_obstacle but for the walkable boundary

openness_ahead.interpretation: dist_to_obstacle sampled at the plan pixel corresponding to 1.5 m ahead in the current heading direction, divided by map maximum. Out-of-bounds → 0 (treated as no clearance).
openness_ahead.reason: Directional affordance ahead: high value means open space, low value means an obstacle is nearby in that direction. Breaks the symmetry of the scalar dist_to_obstacle feature.

openness_left.interpretation: dist_to_obstacle sampled 1.5 m to the left (heading rotated +90°)
openness_left.reason: Directional affordance; allows the model to prefer turns into open space

openness_right.interpretation: dist_to_obstacle sampled 1.5 m to the right (heading rotated −90°)
openness_right.reason: Directional affordance; symmetric counterpart to openness_left

target_du.interpretation: World x displacement at the NEXT timestep (t+1); prediction target
target_du.reason: Predicting displacement rather than absolute position avoids compounding positional error during autoregressive rollout. Strictly next-step to prevent leakage.

target_dv.interpretation: World y displacement at the NEXT timestep (t+1); prediction target
target_dv.reason: Same as target_du for the vertical axis

schema_alterations.reason: Redundant with timestep for sequential modelling. Raw frame indices encode recording-specific artifacts (e.g. frame-rate gaps) rather than motion patterns.
Not available in the distance-field pipeline (requires manual annotation). Entrance proximity can be approximated through position features.

schema_alterations.change: du/dv/speed kept in raw metres, not normalised here
schema_alterations.reason: Normalisation should be deferred to training time using a scaler fitted on the training split only. Pre-normalising would leak dataset statistics into held-out folds.
Obstacle clearance determines forward navigability. Boundary openness is less informative for turn decisions and would double the number of directional features without proportional benefit.

schema_alterations.change: openness_* uses point sampling at lookahead, not ray casting
schema_alterations.reason: The dist_to_obstacle field is precomputed; point sampling is O(1) and sufficient because the field already encodes obstacle proximity at each location. Ray casting would require iterative traversal.
